# Thesis Option Map — Law (Öffentliches Recht), live run 2026-07-04 (Task U re-run)

**Persona (from GT `law.md` full sample interest):** Public law with a focus on
constitutional law, international/European law and human rights, and the legal
regulation of new technologies (AI, data protection, IT law). Methods: doctrinal
legal analysis, comparative/normative analysis. Thesis style: analytical/doctrinal.
No-gos: primary focus on private/civil or criminal law with no public-law dimension;
pure legal history with no contemporary doctrinal engagement.

**Routing:** Juristische Fakultät → Lehrstühle Öffentliches Recht (flat list, no
department drill-down). Pass 1 enumerated all 7 public-law chairs; Pass 2 enriched
every chair — including the multi-strand titles — before any exclusion decision,
per the new §5 "enrich before excluding" rule (Task U).

---

## Interest dimension 1 — Constitutional / International Law & Human Rights

### Lehrstuhl für Staatsrecht, Völkerrecht, Verfassungslehre und Menschenrechte — Prof. Dr. Jochen von Bernstorff, LL.M.
([uni-tuebingen.de](https://uni-tuebingen.de/fakultaeten/juristische-fakultaet/lehrstuehle-und-personen/lehrstuehle/lehrstuehle-oeffentliches-recht/von-bernstorff/))
- Relevant person: Prof. Dr. Jochen von Bernstorff
- Relevance rationale: chair title maps directly onto three of the persona's four
  strands — constitutional law (Staatsrecht/Verfassungslehre), international law
  (Völkerrecht), and human rights (Menschenrechte). Stated focus: general
  international law, theory/history of international-law institutions, prohibition of
  the use of force, humanitarian law.
- Pros & likely difficulties: senior, research-active chair with a strong human-rights
  and international-law profile; no online Masterarbeit announcement found (typical for
  law chairs — direct inquiry needed, not a red flag). Weaker on the tech-regulation
  strand specifically.
- Dated evidence: *L'essor et la chute du droit international humanitaire* (Pedone,
  2024); "The dark legacy of Nuremberg" (*Leiden Journal of International Law*, 2023);
  active DFG project + SFB 932 subproject on land-grabbing and human rights (accessed
  2026-07-04).
- Conversation starter: connect the human-rights/international-law work to the
  regulation of new technologies — e.g. a thesis on human-rights constraints on
  automated decision-making or AI in armed conflict.
- No-go flags: none.

### Lehrstuhl für Staats- und Verwaltungsrecht, Europarecht und Völkerrecht — Prof. Dr. Martin Nettesheim
([uni-tuebingen.de](https://uni-tuebingen.de/fakultaeten/juristische-fakultaet/lehrstuehle-und-personen/lehrstuehle/lehrstuehle-oeffentliches-recht/nettesheim/))
- Relevant person: Prof. Dr. Martin Nettesheim
- Relevance rationale: double match. Chair title covers constitutional (Staatsrecht),
  European (Europarecht) and international (Völkerrecht) law — the persona's core — and
  the stated research areas *also* include **data protection and digital regulation**,
  hitting the tech-regulation strand. Fundamental-rights protection at national/EU/
  international levels is an explicit focus.
- Pros & likely difficulties: prolific, prominent EU-constitutional-law chair;
  competitive and busy. Doctoral/thesis supervision section present but no explicit
  Masterarbeit signal.
- Dated evidence: "GDPR Overreach?" (*Verfassungsblog*, April 2024); "EU Data
  Protection Law and Pay-or-Consent Business Models" (*EU Law Live*, April 2024);
  *Impfpflichten* monograph (2023); ongoing "Risk Sharing in the Euro Area" project
  (accessed 2026-07-04).
- Conversation starter: reference the "GDPR Overreach?" (2024) piece and ask about a
  thesis on the constitutional limits of EU digital/data regulation.
- No-go flags: none.

### Lehrstuhl für Staats- und Verwaltungsrecht, Öffentliches Wirtschaftsrecht, Kommunalrecht — Prof. Dr. Barbara Remmert
([uni-tuebingen.de](https://uni-tuebingen.de/fakultaeten/juristische-fakultaet/lehrstuehle-und-personen/lehrstuehle/lehrstuehle-oeffentliches-recht/remmert/))
- Relevant person: Prof. Dr. Barbara Remmert
- Relevance rationale: the chair *title's* distinguishing strands (Öffentliches
  Wirtschaftsrecht, Kommunalrecht) read economic/municipal law and would suggest
  exclusion on a title-only reading. Pass-2 enrichment of her actual Schwerpunkte shows
  a different picture: her stated research explicitly includes **"Allgemeine
  Grundrechtslehren"** (general fundamental-rights doctrine) and active constitutional
  commentary work — a core match to the persona's constitutional-law + human-rights
  strand that the title alone does not surface. Included per the new §5
  enrich-before-exclude rule.
- Pros & likely difficulties: senior chair-holder with an active constitutional-
  commentary practice; forthcoming publications (2026–2027) suggest an active but
  slow-cadence output — confirm current supervision capacity directly.
- Dated evidence: commentary on Art. 87c–90, 143a–b GG for Beck-online-Kommentar
  (expected May 2026); commentary on Art. 12 Abs. 2, 3 GG in Dürig/Herzog/Scholz
  (manuscript submitted, accessed 2026-07-04) — evidence is forward-dated/in-progress
  rather than already-published; treat as active-but-not-yet-recent and confirm before
  outreach.
- Conversation starter: reference her ongoing Art. 12 GG commentary work and propose a
  thesis connecting general fundamental-rights doctrine to a concrete
  technology-regulation question (e.g. Art. 12 GG occupational-freedom limits on
  AI-driven professional decision-making).
- No-go flags: none.

## Interest dimension 2 — Legal Regulation of New Technologies (AI, data protection, IT law)

### CZS-Stiftungsprofessur für Recht der Künstlichen Intelligenz — Prof. Dr. Michèle Finck, LL.M.
([uni-tuebingen.de](https://uni-tuebingen.de/fakultaeten/juristische-fakultaet/lehrstuehle-und-personen/lehrstuehle/lehrstuehle-oeffentliches-recht/finck/))
- Relevant person: Prof. Dr. Michèle Finck (CZS Foundation Professor for AI Law;
  Director, CZS Institute for AI and Law since Oct 2023)
- Relevance rationale: the direct hit on the tech-regulation strand — AI regulation,
  European data-protection law (GDPR), Data Governance Act, AI in public administration,
  AI explainability. Sits within public law (Öffentliches Recht) so it also anchors the
  persona's public-law framing.
- Pros & likely difficulties: exceptionally active and well-connected (UN Working Group
  on Data Governance; Council of Europe Committee on AI). **⚠ The chair page states she
  currently does not accept new doctoral students** — Masterarbeit supervision is a
  separate question but availability should be confirmed early; a thesis may need to run
  through her institute team.
- Dated evidence: appointed CZS Institute Director Oct 2023; Visiting Professor,
  Dōshisha University Kyoto, March–April 2025; active membership on CoE AI Committee
  (accessed 2026-07-04).
- Conversation starter: reference the Data Governance Act / data-intermediaries work and
  propose a thesis on a concrete AI-regulation question (e.g. explainability duties under
  the AI Act).
- No-go flags: none on topic; availability caveat above.

## Chairs enumerated in Pass 1, enriched, and excluded from the map (topical-justification, §5)

Each of these was Pass-2 enriched (own Schwerpunkte/publications page read) before
exclusion — not dropped on title alone, per the new §5 rule.

- **Prof. Dr. Michael Droege** — title: Verwaltungsrecht, Religionsverfassungs-/
  Kirchenrecht, Steuerrecht. Enrichment: tax/financial constitutional law, third-sector
  law, religious-constitutional law (financing of religious communities, church tax).
  Constitutional dimension present but channeled entirely through
  tax/religion-institutional questions, not the persona's general
  constitutional-law/human-rights/tech-regulation core; no dated evidence found.
  Excluded as adjacent, not core.
- **Prof. Dr. Christian Seiler** — title: Staats-/Verwaltungsrecht, Finanz- und
  Steuerrecht. Enrichment: financial constitution, income/corporate taxation, marriage/
  family status in constitutional-tax-social law, European tax law. Constitutional
  engagement is real but narrowly channeled through fiscal/family policy, not general
  Grundrechtslehre or governance; publication list is dated to March 2020 (stale,
  pre-2022 — fails the §5 date-evidence freshness filter). Excluded on both narrow
  topical fit and stale evidence.
- **Prof. Dr. Johannes Saurer, LL.M. (Yale)** — title: Umweltrecht, Infrastrukturrecht,
  Rechtsvergleichung. Enrichment: chair page confirms environmental/infrastructure law
  + comparative law as the core Schwerpunkte (Schwerpunktbereich 5, "Öffentliche
  Wirtschaft, Infrastruktur und Umwelt"); no constitutional-law, human-rights, or
  tech-regulation focus surfaced on the chair's own page, and no dated publication
  evidence was available to check further. Comparative-law *method* alone is not a
  topical match per §5. **Honest borderline note:** comparative-public-law method is
  adjacent to the persona's international/European-law strand, and this is the
  weakest of the three exclusions — flagged here rather than silently dropped, but not
  promoted to the map without stronger enrichment evidence of a substantive match.

> This map covers publicly visible chairs as of 2026-07-04. Chairs with a weak web

> ask the Fachschaft, and check the official Vorlesungsverzeichnis.
